item.title: SimWin 0.0.4
item.description:
SimWin 0.0.4 Beta

  • Visual Studio support (optional): plugins written for Visual Studio now build too (NuGet packages, C++/WinRT, MSVC-only C++) instead of being left out. Setup asks once; after you accept Microsoft's licence terms it downloads Microsoft's C/C++ runtime and Windows SDK (about 330 MB). Add it later with `simwin setup --visual-studio`.
  • More pub.dev plugins build: small fixes for Windows code that only Microsoft's compiler accepted, applied to SimWin's copy only (your pub cache isn't touched).
  • When a build fails, the run in your IDE stops instead of waiting forever.
  • Out-of-date dependencies are explained: if `flutter pub get` is needed (pubspec changed, Windows plugin folders missing or outdated), SimWin says so instead of showing compiler errors.
  • Uninstall SimWin… in the menu bar and Settings: a progress bar while everything is removed, then a confirmation when SimWin is uninstalled. Or in Terminal: `curl -fsSL https://simwin.dev/uninstall.sh | bash`.
  • Uninstalling now also removes the Windows file associations Wine added to your home folder, and SimWin no longer creates them.
  • Quitting SimWin no longer hangs with SimWin left in the Dock when a Windows app doesn't stop.
  • Help in Settings lists every `simwin` command.
  • Setup shows download speed and time left, and continues where it stopped if you close its window.
  • "SimWin · Windows 11" stays in your IDE's device list: SimWin turns Flutter's custom devices back on and re-registers itself if SimWin.app moved.
  • The simulator and your app move together when you drag the window, and stay together when other apps' windows are in between.
  • Signed with Developer ID and notarized by Apple. Universal (Apple Silicon and Intel), macOS 14 or later.

item.title: SimWin 0.0.3
item.description:
• Performance profiler: a live readout on the taskbar (frame rate, frame time, CPU and memory) and a Performance panel (Window ▸ Performance…, ⌥⌘P) with frame timings, CPU and memory charts, what your app, the runtime and SimWin each use, and startup times. Record a session and export it as CSV or JSON. Works when the IDE is attached, too.
  • Projects without a windows folder: instead of a build error, SimWin offers to enable Windows for the project, as your IDE does for iOS and Android. Nothing changes until you click Enable Windows.
  • Export logs: save the log as a text file or all of SimWin's logs as a zip (Export in the log view, or Export Logs… in the menu bar).
  • The simulator window can no longer be made smaller than your app.
  • Lighter on your Mac: while no app runs, SimWin's Windows background processes now use about 0.2% CPU and 63 MB (was 1.3% and 83 MB), and the performance readout uses about half the CPU it did. App logs on disk stop at 10 MB.
  • Stopping an app from your IDE no longer shows "quit unexpectedly (exit code 143)".
  • Changing the scale, language or profile (or Relaunch) no longer makes the simulator disappear while the app restarts: it stays where it is and says what it is applying, for example "Applying 125% scale…".
  • SimWin no longer leaves processes running. Quitting ends everything it started: builds, your app and the Windows background services, including when you quit while a build or launch is still in progress. If SimWin crashes or is force-quit, it cleans up what was left the next time it opens. Previously these could keep using memory and CPU until you restarted your Mac.
  • Redesigned About window, and a simpler setup with one progress bar.
  • Anonymous usage statistics (which features are used and how builds go) help us improve SimWin. Never your code, project names or file paths. Turn it off in Settings ▸ Share anonymous usage data. Details: https://simwin.dev/privacy/
  • Licence Agreement updated to version 1.1 (privacy section).
  • Signed with Developer ID and notarized by Apple. Universal (Apple Silicon and Intel), macOS 14 or later.

item.title: SimWin 0.0.2
item.description:
SimWin 0.0.2 Beta

SimWin is now in beta, for Windows debug builds only. Version numbers restart at 0.0.x for the beta; if you have 0.1.0, this update is newer and installs as usual.

  • The simulator is a Windows-style desktop with a SimWin wallpaper, a taskbar, a Start menu and quick settings. Your app runs inside it, as one window with the simulator, with no separate Dock icon.
  • Real Windows title bar: minimise goes to the taskbar, maximise fills the simulator's desktop, and restore and close work as on Windows.
  • Wi-Fi switch in the taskbar (or simwin network off) to test offline handling; the debugger stays connected.
  • Apps you've run appear as desktop icons. Double-click to build and run; right-click to Run, Show in Finder or Remove from Desktop.
  • SimWin opens to the simulator, with ▶ to run a recent project and ⚙ for Settings.
  • Faster runs: SimWin keeps Wine warm between runs (about 9 s instead of 16 s on our test Mac).
  • No more Wine error dialogs when an app closes. If an app quits unexpectedly, SimWin tells you, with Show Logs and Report a Problem.
  • Changing the display scale or locale keeps your app in front.
  • New About window with Check for Updates and readable acknowledgements, and the SimWin Licence Agreement (Help ▸ Licence Agreement).
  • Signed with Developer ID and notarized by Apple. Universal (Apple Silicon and Intel), macOS 14 or later.

item.title: SimWin 0.1.0
item.description:
SimWin 0.1.0, the first release.

  • Run the Windows debug build of your Flutter app on your Mac, as the IDE device “SimWin · Windows 11”.
  • Hot reload, hot restart, breakpoints and DevTools.
  • Toolbar for display scale, window size, light or dark mode and locale; screenshots and recordings.
  • Help ▸ Report a Problem… to send us diagnostics.
  • Signed with Developer ID and notarized by Apple. Universal (Apple Silicon and Intel), macOS 14 or later.
